alt: Murdock’s four universal functions (sexual, reproductive, economic, educational) narrow through structural differentiation to Parsons’s two irreducible functions: primary socialisation and stabilisation of adult personalities.
caption: Industrial society strips the family to two functions that matter more than ever.

alt: Parsons argued the isolated nuclear family fits industrial society because it is geographically and socially mobile and has a clear instrumental and expressive division of labour. Laslett and Anderson challenge the history.
caption: Historical evidence questions whether industry created the nuclear family.

alt: Four Marxist arguments: Engels on inheritance of property, Althusser on the family as an ideological state apparatus, the family as a unit of consumption, and Zaretsky’s haven that props up capitalism, with evaluation.
caption: For Marxists, the family reproduces class inequality and makes capitalism bearable.

alt: A grid of liberal, Marxist, radical and Black or intersectional feminisms, each with its key argument about families and a sociologist: Oakley, Benston, Delphy and Leonard, and bell hooks.
caption: Feminists agree families shape gender inequality but disagree on why.

alt: A grid comparing functionalism, Marxism and feminisms on who benefits from the family, socialisation, domestic roles, view of change and main weakness.
caption: Ask whose needs the family meets: society’s, capitalism’s or men’s.

alt: Each point names a mechanism, the sociologist and the consequence for capitalism: inheritance of property (Engels) reproduces class inequality; the ideological apparatus (Althusser) legitimises capitalism.
caption: Mechanism, sociologist, consequence: every time.
